1.why: Set offers contrast/restatement/temporal/causal; 'Meanwhile' is a throwaway and 'In other words' needs a restatement, so the causal 'Thus' is the likeliest key.

2.why: Pure number-swap set - all four compare both conditions, so no option text distinguishes them; picked the mid-range pair.

3.why: 'In short' and 'Instead' are narrow; 'Nevertheless' is the standard concessive key against a filler 'Meanwhile'.

4.why: All four state a median and a strongest predictor; chose the largest, most emphatic magnitude ('92 seconds fast') as fitting 'emphasize the main finding'.

5.why: 'To be sure' and 'Meanwhile' are weak fillers; 'Consequently' is the causal option and 'In addition' would need pure addition.

6.why: Only the numbers vary across the same sentence frame; genuinely undecidable, took the largest throughput/rescan spread.

7.why: Set has one addition, one contrast, one causal, one exemplifier; 'For instance' is the one that a following specific case would demand.

8.why: Same four-category spread as item 7; 'For example' is the least substitutable of the four and 'Meanwhile' is filler.

9.why: 'Still' is the concessive in a set whose other members ('Meanwhile', 'Instead', 'For instance') are each narrowly conditioned.

10.why: Strongest treatment-vs-control divergence (52 to 9 percent while the untreated pond rose), which is what 'emphasize the main finding' rewards.

11.why: 'In other words' is the restatement option; 'Instead' and 'Nevertheless' both need an explicit negation the stem type rarely supplies.

12.why: Only B names two independent caveats that both bite - a biased sampling window ('busiest period') and a measurement gap ('whether a passerby actually bought anything').

13.why: Largest predicted-vs-measured gap (26% vs 9%) with a cause about the dust itself rather than an external rinse; best fits 'why the finding surprised'.

14.why: All four hedge identically; A pairs the small n with the clearest confound (raised beds on a sunnier south wall), which is what makes the summary cautious.

15.why: 'In that case' and 'Regardless' are rare keys; 'By comparison' is the natural pairing word against a bare 'Instead'.

16.why: 'Namely' and 'Consequently' are narrow; 'However' is the contrast option in an otherwise additive set.

17.why: 'Beforehand' and 'Granted' are implausible keys; 'As a result' beats 'By comparison', which needs an explicit second case.

18.why: 'Even so' is the only concessive against three additive/causal options ('As a result', 'In particular', 'Also').

19.why: 'If so' and 'Even then' need a hypothetical antecedent; 'In practice' is the standard theory-to-reality pivot.

20.why: 'In the meantime' is filler and the causal/contrast options are covered twice over; 'For example' is the exemplifier the set is built around.

21.why: 'By contrast' is the pairing word; 'If so' is a weak conditional distractor and 'Nevertheless' duplicates the contrast slot more weakly.

22.why: 'Otherwise' and 'Instead' both require a negated prior clause; 'By contrast' is the cleaner contrastive key over the additive 'What is more'.

23.why: 'Specifically' is the elaboration option; 'Likewise' and 'For this reason' need matching or causal setups, and 'Admittedly' a concession.

24.why: 'However' is the lone contrast among three reinforcing options ('For instance', 'Indeed', 'Similarly').
